headline: Surgeons in Xi'an, China, have carried out what China Daily calls the third robotic-arm heart transplant in the world, working through a small cut between the ribs instead of splitting the breastbone.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a notable medical use of robots, but it is one patient reported by the hospital's own surgeons and the operation was on 5 Oct 2026.
importance_line: Heart failure patients too frail for open surgery could benefit if the method proves safe, but this is a single case from one state-run outlet and the technique is still at an early stage.
summary: China Daily reports that on 5 Oct 2026 surgeons at the First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University transplanted a donor heart into a 67-year-old man with end-stage heart failure, using robotic arms through an 8-centimeter cut between the ribs without splitting the breastbone, which it describes as a first in China and the third in the world. Yan Yang, director of cardiovascular surgery at the hospital, says the patient came off the ventilator the same day and now walks daily, and that robotic heart transplantation is still at an early, exploratory stage.
notes: Surgery on 5 Oct 2026; the report on 16 Oct 2026 appears to be the first public one (only China Daily found), so the main session may prefer to treat it as NEW. Robotic arms are operated by the surgeon (teleoperated surgery), not autonomous; machine_action true because the robot performs the operation under his control. Third in the world, after Saudi Arabia (2024) and the United States (2025), per China Daily.
